name: SG Mart Ltd
title: SG Mart Ltd - 512329 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SG Mart Q2 FY27 EBITDA of INR72 crore; H1 EBITDA INR131 crore, with management reaffirming INR300 crore FY27 target.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 FY27 EBITDA was INR72 crore, the third consecutive quarter of sustained performance, and H1 EBITDA reached INR131 crore. HR coil processing volume was 206,000 tons (up 16% QoQ) and profile volume about 40,000 tons (up 20% QoQ). Capex was INR250 crore in H1, funded from internal cash, with cash on books around INR700 crore. Management reiterated 25%+ ROC, a 6-7% blended EBITDA margin ambition versus 4-5% now, and a 50%+ earnings CAGR over three to four years.

financial_highlights.change: Third consecutive quarter of sustained performance; no change stated vs Q1
H1 earnings stated as up 100% YoY

segments.name: Service centre / trading
segments.commentary: Eight service centres operational (Ghaziabad, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Pune, Bangalore, Raipur, Indore added this quarter); pure service centre sales up 30% YoY per management. Service centre EBITDA about INR2,000 per ton, stable QoQ; processing margin 3-4%.

segments.name: Profiles (steel profiles and solar structures)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 40,000 tons, up 20% QoQ; annual capacity cited as half a million tons. Solar order book above 50,000 tons with about one-year visibility; steel profiles EBITDA INR4,000-5,000 per ton and solar structures INR3,000-4,000 per ton, both stable QoQ.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: Five products launched, two to three more in process; management described the segment as stable and profitable, selling through the same distribution channel. No quantitative disclosure given.

segments.name: Dubai service centre
segments.commentary: Volume stagnant QoQ; margins slightly better due to steel scarcity while ports remain closed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA target of INR300 crore maintained; H2 requires about INR170 crore (about INR80 crore per quarter run rate), which management said is achievable.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to rise to 6-7% from 4-5% as Raipur backward integration plant (coated steel) starts in 9-12 months, adding 200-300 bps.
Management maintained 50%+ earnings CAGR for the next three to four years; ROC target about 25%, with over 30% possible once capacities are fully utilised.
Service centre target raised to 30-35 by 2030 from 25+; management hinted at faster openings. Plan adds five to six centres a year, with the next batch of two to three due by April-May 2027.

Online sales platform to be ready in about six months; capex of INR250-300 crore for rest of FY27 plus about INR1,500 crore over the next two to three years, funded from internal cash and cash on books, with no debt planned.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR250 crore in H1 FY27 for land, service centre plant and equipment, and Raipur plant.
Remaining FY27 capex INR250-300 crore; further about INR1,500 crore over next two to three years to complete service centres and Raipur manufacturing plant.

Per service centre: land about INR50 crore (10-acre parcel), plant and machinery about INR5 crore, shed about INR10 crore; total INR70-80 crore, generating monthly revenue of about INR70-80 crore at 3-4% EBITDA margin.
Each service centre capacity about 12,000-13,000 tons per month (8,000 tons HR coil processing, 1,000-2,000 tons CRCA, 2,000-3,000 tons pre-galvanised); 25 centres imply about 3.5 million tons.

Profile capacity half a million tons per year, with business plan to scale capacities 3-4x over five years. Service centres take 6-9 months to fully ramp up. Steel volume processed about 1-1.5 million tons per year.
demand_pricing: Steel prices rose 25-30% over the past 6-7 months since Middle East crisis, which management said is denting end demand in construction, automobile and white goods.
Ocean freight costs have risen sharply, hurting customers involved in international trade; crude and commodity prices weighing on sentiment.
Solar order book above 50,000 tons with about one-year visibility, after bookings were held back during steel price rises; October saw significant new orders.
CRCA sheets realise INR2,000-3,000 per ton over HR coil; management expects 1,000-2,000 tons per month per service centre.
Dealer and distributor base about 1,200; PEB customers include top 100 PEB companies buying from service centres.
Management said steel price stability and resolution of IPP land-acquisition delays helped solar orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is service centre ramp-up slower than guidance; is land acquisition the bottleneck?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ramp-up is better than expected and it may open faster, possibly reaching 30-35 centres by 2030 instead of 25+. No bottleneck was specifically named.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 7% margin apply only to profiles?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the 6-7% margin is for the whole company on a blended basis, from 4-5% now (H1 at 4.5%), with processing at 3-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q2 include inventory gains from higher steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Inventory is about 14-15 days with 15-20 churns a year, so management said it avoids steel price gains and losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR300 crore EBITDA guidance be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. H1 is INR131 crore, so H2 needs INR170 crore, or about INR80 crore a quarter, which management said is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising interest rates and macro factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited steel price spikes, freight and crude sentiment as macro headwinds to demand, but said they do not expect major impact on growth. It is cautious, holds low inventory and avoids debt.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton and product mix levers apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Service centre about INR2,000 per ton; steel profiles INR4,000-5,000; solar INR3,000-4,000, all stable QoQ. Coated steel backward integration adds high-margin product mix, plus same-store growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new product line (welding rods, wire mesh, etc.) made in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently bought from third-party factories; in-house lines to follow once volumes scale, with a decision in about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of a service centre and when does it break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment INR70-80 crore, monthly revenue INR70-80 crore at 3-4% EBITDA, 25%+ ROC with 18 working capital days. Backward-integrated Raipur products expected to add margin in 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Demand softness from steel price spike, freight costs and weaker sentiment in construction, auto and white goods.
Execution of Raipur backward integration plant (9-12 months) needed for margin uplift to 6-7%.
H2 EBITDA must reach about INR170 crore to meet INR300 crore FY27 target.
Capex of about INR1,500 crore more over the next two to three years; cash on books down to about INR700 crore.
Dubai operations depend on port reopening and steel supply; expansion there deferred until the crisis ends.
Online platform and contract manufacturing plans still at early stage with no quantified targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume ramp-up, margin expansion and the FY27 EBITDA target, but cautious on macro headwinds from steel prices and freight. Management gave few hard numbers on accessories, online sales and contract manufacturing, and deferred several questions.
key_quotes: So, we are fairly confident that this business model of combining the distribution the trading with manufacturing and manufacturing with backward integration, it's a very unique positioning what we are building in the country
We don't see macro factors impacting us too much that could derail our growth in the coming quarters.
We are pretty confident that the ROC profile we should be able to maintain around 25% which is our target in the coming years.

adds.what: Service centres: next batch of two to three due by April-May 2027 (five to six centres a year planned)

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA target of INR300 crore held, requiring INR170 crore in H2 (about INR80 crore per quarter), backed by eight operational service centres, the solar order book above 50,000 tons and Raipur coated-steel plant starting in 9-12 months, though no quantified capacity addition or timing is given for the FY27 EBITDA target itself.
